## v0.4.1 — Balance & Settlements

A new country no longer goes broke in half an hour, and a large one no longer hits the treasury limit in two cycles. Land now costs more the bigger the country is, and colonies and villages of two popular mods become part of it.

### ⏱️ Shorter Cycle, Daily Report
- The economy cycle is **3 minutes** instead of 8⅓, so a new tax block pays off almost at once.
- No more chat message after every cycle, and no salary message every 3 minutes. Instead, **at dawn** every citizen gets one report for the past day: income, expenses, net and the treasury, with a breakdown by source on hover (ⓘ). Leaders also see unpaid salaries and money lost to a full treasury; players see their salary and plot rent for the day.
- Turn the report off with `economyDailyReport`. Without the daylight cycle a report comes every 20 minutes of play.
- Amounts per cycle are smaller to match, so the economy per hour stays the same. Loans may now last up to 140 cycles (7 hours, as before), and wallets keep the last 50 operations instead of 20.

### ⚖️ Economy Balance

| | 0.4 | 0.4.1 |
|---|---|---|
| Economy cycle | 8⅓ min | **3 min** |
| Treasury of a new country | 1 000$ | **2 500$** (`startingTreasury`) |
| Upkeep per chunk | 10$ per cycle (72$/h) | **2$** per cycle (40$/h); the first 9 chunks (the capital's core) are free |
| Upkeep of the 25 founding chunks | 1 800$/h | **640$/h** |
| Income per tax block | 50$ per cycle (360$/h) | **16$** per cycle (320$/h) |
| Tax blocks per chunk | 4 | **2** |
| Embassy | 100$ per cycle (720$/h) | **40$** per cycle (800$/h) |

- A starting country now breaks even with two tax blocks instead of five, and has about four hours instead of half an hour to set them up.
- The ceiling on income is lower: a fully taxed chunk brings 640$ instead of 1 440$ per hour, so the treasury limit is no longer reached right after founding.

### 🗺️ Cost of New Territory
- **The price grows with the country.** A chunk costs 300$ while the country has up to 25 chunks; each chunk above that makes the next one 2% dearer, up to 5 000$. That is 450$ at 50 chunks, 750$ at 100 and 1 350$ at 200.
- **Outposts cost ×3.** A chunk that does not touch the country's land costs three times more.
- The **Map** tab shows what the selected chunks will cost before buying, including outposts. Connected chunks are bought in an order that touches the country, so a selection next to the border never counts as outposts.
- A mayor who adds a chunk to their own city from the Map tab now pays from the city treasury, like with `/politicsmod claim <city>`; before, the nation paid.
- New config keys: `startingTreasury`, `chunkPriceGrowthPercent`, `chunkPriceGrowthStart`, `maxChunkPrice`, `outpostPriceMultiplier`, `upkeepFreeChunks`.
- **Existing servers:** values still at the 0.4 defaults are replaced with the new ones on the first start; values you changed yourself stay as they are. A server with its own cycle length keeps its own amounts per cycle.

### 🏘️ MineColonies and Millénaire (NeoForge)
Both mods are optional and work for Minecraft 1.21.1 on NeoForge (MineColonies 1.1, Millénaire 9 — tested with 9.0.2). Colonies and villages become part of political life instead of standing beside it.
- **New Settlements tab** in the country dashboard (shown when either mod is on the server): every colony and village of the country with its population, happiness or reputation, tax and location, plus the villages it may annex. They are also marked on the Map tab. `/politicsmod settlement` lists them in chat.
- **Colonies belong to their owner's country.** A colony of a citizen pays 4$ per colonist every cycle (`colonyTaxPerCitizen`), more when the colonists are happy: ×0.5 at happiness 0, ×1.5 at 10 (`colonyTaxFollowsHappiness`).

## v0.4 — Survival & Property

Until now, money and land belonged only to countries. In 0.4 every player gets their own — and countries get real politics: elections, laws, sieges and debt.

### 🚀 New Features

**New Country Dashboard (`K`)**
- One style for every screen: a sidebar with seven tabs — Overview, Map, Citizens, Politics, Diplomacy, Economy and News. The Protection, Trade Warehouse, founding and Residential Building screens use the same look.
- Built for small windows: every label fits in all 12 languages down to 1366×768 at GUI scale 3; long descriptions wrap, and law descriptions show in full on hover.
- **Overview:** flag, capital, key numbers (treasury, citizens, territory, net per cycle), cities with mayors and treasuries, laws, election, wars and debt at a glance.
- **Map:** bigger map with zoom (mouse wheel), a legend, and colours for your land, your cities, allies, enemies and other countries. Hover a chunk to see its owner. The old "Unclaim (Wilderness)" button, which actually claimed land, is now correctly named "Claim for country".

**Elections**
- The leader calls an election for leader or for a city's mayor. Citizens run (`/politicsmod election run`) and vote (`/politicsmod election vote <name>`) until the timer ends; the winner takes office.
- A petition signed by half of the citizens starts a leader election by itself.

**Laws**
- **Closed Borders:** only citizens may enter (enemies at war still can).
- **Martial Law:** lower tax income, but sieges against the country take twice as long.
- **Free Trade:** more embassy income, and no market fee between free-trade countries.
- `/politicsmod law enact|repeal <law>` or the Politics tab. Laws can't be changed too often.

**Sieges**
- Border chunks are no longer free to break during a war. Instead, start a siege in an enemy border chunk (`/politicsmod siege start`, costs money).
- Progress grows while more attackers than defenders stand in the chunk; hold it until the boss bar fills and the chunk is yours. With no attackers for a while, the siege fails.
- Attackers can break blocks only in the chunk they are besieging.

**Debt and Loans**
- Treasuries can go into debt (down to a configurable limit). A bankrupt country can't declare war or start sieges, and its mayors may secede whatever the tax.
- Allies lend each other money with interest: `/politicsmod loan offer <amount> <interest> <cycles> <country>`, then `accept`, `reject` or `list`. Installments are paid every economy cycle.

**News Feed**
- Foundings, wars, peace, alliances, elections, laws, sieges, loans and bankruptcies are recorded. `/politicsmod news` or the News tab.

**Flagpole**
- A new block that flies the flag of the country owning the land, waving in the wind. It changes by itself when the land changes hands.
- A white enamel pole with an iron foot and a gold finial; its own inventory icon.

**Borders in the World**
- The tall pillars are gone. A border is now a thin line lying on the ground and following the terrain, with a soft coloured strip on the inner side.
- Your country is green, your city gold, allies blue, enemies at war red, other countries their own colour. City borders inside a country are fainter.
- Styles (`/politicsmod borders style`): line on the ground (default), glowing fence that fades upwards, dashed line. Borders fade out with distance.

**Maps**
- Country borders on **BlueMap** and **Dynmap** web maps and on the **JourneyMap** minimap, when those mods are installed. Nothing extra is needed otherwise. (Xaero's maps have no public API.)

**Personal Wallet**
- Every player has a wallet: `/politicsmod wallet` shows the balance and history.
- Send money to any player (even offline), donate to your country's treasury.
- The wallet is shown in the HUD.

**Five New Languages**
- **Portuguese (Brazil)**, **Portuguese (Portugal)**, **Italian**, **Chinese (Simplified)** and **Japanese**. PoliticsMod now speaks 12 languages.

**Salaries & Income Tax**

releases.notes:
# Changelog

## v0.3 — Fabric, Market & Management

### 🚀 New Features

**Fabric Support**
- PoliticsMod now runs on **Fabric** as well as **NeoForge** (Minecraft 1.21.1), built from a single codebase with Architectury.

**Trade Warehouse — Inter-Country Market**
- The Trade Warehouse has been completely reworked into a **global market between nations**.
- **Selling:** any citizen can list the item in their hand for a price. The item is held by the market until it's sold or withdrawn.
- **Buying:** leaders and mayors buy goods from other nations with the treasury. Items go straight to the buyer's inventory, and the money goes to the seller's treasury.
- **Diplomacy matters:** nations at war can't trade (**embargo**). Allies trade **without the market fee**.
- The seller's online citizens are notified of every sale.
- Listings are stored in world data, so breaking a warehouse doesn't remove your goods.

**Server Configuration**
- New `config/politicsmod.json` with **18 settings**: claim prices, upkeep, tax income, economy cycle length, war cost and cooldown, vault and embassy bonuses, radar range, and market fee and limits.
- Invalid values are corrected automatically, and missing keys are added after updates.
- New command: `/politicsmod reload` reloads the config without a restart (operators only).

### 🎮 Gameplay & Security

**Survival Support (first step)**
- The Trade Warehouse now works in **Survival mode**: it has a crafting recipe (chest, gold ingots and planks), drops when broken, and is mined faster with an axe.
- Other PoliticsMod blocks remain Creative-only for now.

**Anti-Exploit Protection**
- All market actions are validated on the server: role, treasury funds, embargo and listing availability.
- Items are removed from the player's hand at the moment of listing, so they can't be duplicated.
- Market actions only work while standing next to a warehouse.

### 🖥️ UI & Localization

**Dashboard Overhaul (`K`)**
- Three new tabs:
  - **Citizens:** member list with roles and online status. Invite, kick, and promote or demote mayors.
  - **Diplomacy:** relations with every nation. Declare war, propose an alliance or peace, and accept or reject incoming proposals.
  - **Economy:** treasury and limit, income breakdown (tax blocks, federal tax, embassies), upkeep, tribute and net result per cycle. Leaders can adjust the federal tax rate with ±1/±5 buttons.
- Actions are shown according to your role and follow exactly the same rules as the chat commands.

**Market Screen**
- New Trade Warehouse interface with **Market** and **Our Listings** tabs, item tooltips and pagination.

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **Fixed a crash on dedicated servers** during startup (`invalid dist DEDICATED_SERVER`) caused by client-side GUI classes being loaded on the server.
- Fixed `/politicsmod info` showing an incorrect net income: it ignored embassy bonuses and counted city tax blocks as national income. It now matches the actual economy cycle.
- Fixed claim prices being defined separately for the `/politicsmod claim` command and the map GUI, which could make them disagree.
- Fixed claim messages showing hardcoded amounts (500$ / 100$) instead of the real price.
- Fixed player roles appearing in Russian on the dashboard regardless of game language.

### ⚠️ Important Notes

- **New required dependency:** [Architectury API](https://modrinth.com/mod/architectury-api) on both loaders. Fabric also requires **Fabric API**. **GeckoLib** is still required.
- **The old 27-slot Trade Warehouse has been removed.** Any items stored in previously placed warehouses will be lost.

releases.notes:
v0.2 - The Civilization Update

Infrastructure Blocks

  • Tax Block: Generates +50$ per economic cycle. Up to 4 blocks per chunk. Income is routed to the city treasury (if the chunk belongs to a city) or the country treasury directly.
  • Embassy: Links to a partner country via /politicsmod embassy link <country>. While not at war, each active embassy grants +100$ per cycle. Right-click the block to inspect its current link status and income. Now backed by a full BlockEntity that persists the link across restarts.
  • Radar Tower: Scans a 5-chunk radius every ~5 seconds. When enemies (players from countries at war) are detected, a warning is pushed to all online members via the HUD overlay. Alert fades automatically after 5 seconds.
  • Vault / Bank: Raises the country treasury cap by +10,000$ per vault placed. Right-click to inspect the vault's reserve and the current treasury limit. Now backed by a BlockEntity with its own reserve field — groundwork for future deposit mechanics.

Diplomacy System

  • War: Costs 500$ to declare; 10-minute cooldown between declarations. Enemies may break blocks on border chunks during wartime.
  • Alliance: Mutual PvP protection; allied players cannot damage each other.
  • Peace: Requires both sides to accept via a proposal/accept flow.
  • Surrender & Tribute: Losing country pays 20% of income per cycle to the victor. Tribute can be forgiven by the receiving country at any time.
  • Territory Purchase: Countries can make buy offers on foreign chunks; the owner accepts or rejects in-place.

Economy System

Automated financial cycle runs every ~8 minutes:

  • Tax Collection: Tax Block income collected and routed to city or country treasury.
  • Federal Tax: Deducted from each city and forwarded to the national treasury.
  • Territory Upkeep: -10$ per owned chunk charged each cycle.
  • Tribute Payments: Processed automatically between countries at war.
  • Embassy Bonuses: Applied per cycle (skipped if at war with the linked country).
  • Balance Cap: Capped at 10,000$ + (vaults × 10,000$).

City & Governance Expansion

  • Mayors: Leaders can appoint mayors per city via /politicsmod city setmayor. Mayors manage their city's expansion from the city treasury.
  • City Treasuries: Each city maintains its own balance, fed by Tax Block income and drained by city chunk claims.
  • Federal Tax Rate: Configurable 0–99% via /politicsmod tax federal <rate>. At ≥ 80%, mayors unlock the right to secede.
  • City Secession: A mayor under oppressive taxation can found a fully independent state via /politicsmod city secede, provided the city treasury holds ≥ 100$.

Territory & Player Protection

  • Block Protection: Block breaking is protected per chunk — only Citizens, Mayors, and Leaders of the owning country may build. Exception: enemies may break blocks on border chunks during wartime.
  • Container & Door Access: Interaction blocked for non-citizens on foreign territory at all times.
  • Friendly Fire: Disabled between allied countries.

HUD & Client Improvements

releases.notes:
### New Features
* **State Management:** Added **Founding Stone** to create countries and **City Stone** to establish cities.
* **Territory System:** Implemented chunk claiming with visual borders (Lines, Walls, Corners).
* **Economy & Population:** Added **Residential Building** for population simulation.
* **Commands:** Added `/politicscraft delete` to dissolve your nation (with confirmation).

### Gameplay & Security
* **Creative Only:** Strictly disabled block interactions and breaking in Survival mode for security on RP servers.
* **Anti-Duplicate:** Prevented players from creating multiple countries.

### UI & Localization
* **Dashboard:** Added a comprehensive GUI for managing nations and cities.
* **HUD:** Added an overlay showing the current country, city, and balance.
* **Languages:** Added full localization for **English and Russian**.
